Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

hand noun

the cards a player holds

also hand of cards

Renaissance

M-O s.v. card: hand, from Vives 1540
Andresian p. 16

lūdus, lūdī m.

noun, second declension

Vives’s use: the cards one has to play with. Of a player with the better hand he writes superiōrem habet lūdum tuō.

Examples

  • Lūdum habeō dissipātum et male cohaerentem — cēdō tibi.

    My hand is all over the place and doesn’t hang together — I pass.Vives, Exercitātiō (1540) p. 382, quoted by Morgan–Owens s.v. card: hand

See also card game, playing card, dealer.

SourcesLewis & Short: ludus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. card: hand; pass.
